newsitem.title: USA: NYS comptroller proposes block grants for schools.
newsitem.headline: NYS comptroller proposes block grants for schools.

text.p: The New York State comptroller on Wednesday proposed funding the state's public schools with with block grants and reforming property taxes to help equalize how much different schools get.
However, H. Carl McCall, noting that local property taxes raise about $15 billion for schools, said that the state cannot afford to take on this burden.
"As such, replacing it would require a major increase in state taxes, damaging New York's competitiveness with other states. We just can't afford it," he said, in prepared remarks.

McCall also said efforts to freeze property taxes while understandable were "impractical (and) unaffordable," adding this method would hurt local autonomy and worsen disparities between school districts.
The current way the state distributes aid to schools was intended to help smooth out differences between how much schools in poorer and richer areas get.

However, McCall, saying that objective has not been met, proposed that the state instead consider using block grants to give districts more flexibility. He also proposed giving districts incentives to economize, saying that the present method actually encourages them to spend more.
The Business Council of New York, a lobbying group, said it backed the comptroller's efforts to use block grants and focus on cost-effectiveness.

"Over the last generation or so, New York State has gotten a bad deal in public education. Costs, by any measure, have skyrocketed; quality if anything, has deteriorated," said Anthony Moro, president of Power Capital and chairman of the council's education committee, in prepared remarks.
